title: Off the Mark
intro: Getting to the ball on time starts with your first two steps, and you can train them. Every start here is one you choose, so go flat out and take the full rest after each one. It's sixteen starts, about ninety-two metres of running in all. If you haven't done any jump work lately, do Landing Gear first, because every split-step here is a landing.

You need a court or about twenty-five metres of flat, non-slip ground, and court shoes. Mark each distance with tape or a line, not cones or bags you could step on. Run through the end of every start and slow down over the next ten metres. Do it on fresh legs early in the day, never as a finisher. If your starts get slower than the ones before, end the session there.

before.label: Not today
before.text: A sore ankle, knee, calf, hamstring, groin or Achilles, or an injury in the last month? Get it looked at first.

before.label: Stop and get it checked
before.text: A sharp pain, pain that spreads, numbness, swelling, a joint that gives way, or a sudden pull or pop.

before.label: Stop now
before.text: Chest pain, dizziness, a heartbeat that races or skips, or breathing that doesn't feel right. Get it looked at before you train again. Told to be careful with hard exercise? Check with your doctor first.

before.label: Past injury
before.text: Ever torn a knee ligament, or coming back from an ankle injury? Ask whoever treated you if starts and cuts are OK.

before.label: Keep clear
before.text: 48 hours away from another hard session, and not the day before a match.

before.label: First time
before.text: Do two sets of each start instead of four.

good: Jog easy until you're warm and breathing a little harder
Feel your legs loosen up with every minute
Hold a wall and swing the leg front to back, then side to side
Feel the hip loosen up as the swing gets bigger
bad: Arching your lower back to throw the leg higher

good: Step wide and sit back into that hip, chest tall
Feel the inside of the straight leg stretch
bad: Letting the bent knee cave inward

good: Step long, drop the back hip, then reach the inside arm up to the ceiling
Feel the front of the back hip and your upper back open up
bad: Rushing the reach before the hips have dropped

good: Tall hips, and strike the ground right underneath you
Feel a light, springy bounce off the ball of the foot
bad: Reaching the foot out in front of your body

good: Add speed on each run, about 60, then 80, then 90 percent of your top speed
Fast but relaxed, never straining
bad: Going flat out on the first one

good: Land the split-step loaded, then explode toward the spot you picked
Your legs pushing the ground back behind you
bad: Landing the split-step with narrow feet and straight knees

good: Turn your hips toward the side you're going and cross the far leg over as you push off the other
Your hips turning before your feet move
bad: Twisting on a planted foot instead of turning your hips

good: Open your hip and step back with the foot on the side you're going, then drive off it
Feel your hip turn first and the push come second
Split-step, then drive forward and diagonally toward the net
A strong push off the back leg
bad: Reaching your front foot out on the first step
